claims.statement: In their first fight, Tom Allen was beating Mike McCoole when the crowd broke into the ring, and the referee then gave McCoole the win on a foul.
claims.excerpt: Allen was giving Mike a bad whipping when the crowd broke into the ring

claims.statement: Tom Allen defeated Mike McCoole in their return match, which was advertised as a championship fight, on an island in the Mississippi opposite St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: as was their return match, in which Allen was an easy victor
places: Island in the Mississippi opposite St. Louis

claims.statement: Titles were nebulous in those days, and Tom Allen had only a thin claim to the heavyweight title.
claims.excerpt: Titles, in those days, were nebulous, however, and Allen had only a thin claim to it

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss to a 35-round draw before leaving England.
claims.excerpt: Allen had fought a 35-round draw with Joe Goss

claims.statement: In 1876 Joe Goss beat Tom Allen in Kentucky on a foul after 29 rounds, and Allen lost all claim to the title.
claims.excerpt: years later when, in 1876, they fought in Kentucky, Goss winning on a foul after 29 rounds

claims.statement: Tom Allen was 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighed under 175 pounds.
claims.excerpt: He was only 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighed under 175 pounds

fights.excerpt: Allen was giving Mike a bad whipping when the crowd broke into the ring
fights.notes: Referee declared McCoole the winner on a foul; McCoole then claimed the title. Undated in this text.
